notes: Copilot's oversized-line cell. Copilot records are FAT relative to their token count — a measured assistant.message carried content=156 chars but reasoningOpaque=416 B + base64 encryptedContent=7,720 B at 764 outputTokens (9,339-byte line); the largest real line seen on this machine is 31,953 B (system.message). A 5,000-word single-sentence reply therefore extrapolates to tens-to-hundreds of KB — the buffered accumulateChunk path in core/pkg/tailer/line_reader.go, well under both the 64 MB maxTranscriptLineSize and bufio.Scanner's old 2 MB limit. So, like the claudecode sibling, this is a sanity check rather than true cap-stress, and the absence of a parser stall is INFERRED from the arc completing. Copilot is structurally more robust than claudecode here: the settle rides on assistant.turn_end (max 185 bytes), a record separate from the giant assistant.message, so even the errLineTooLong discard branch would still fire working→ready. PRESESSION SHAPE (as for basic-turn): session-state/<id>/ holds only workspace.yaml at launch and events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a proc-<PID> row first and the real session arrives under a DIFFERENT id — birth is two phases and every later phase anchors to the REAL session. turn_end anchors to turn_start so the matcher picks the post-turn ready rather than the birth ready. OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map; model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
Real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, born ready
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
The long-reply prompt lands as user.message → ready → working on the real session

The oversized assistant.message line is buffered and parsed (or, above the 64 MB cap, skipped past) and assistant.turn_end settles working → ready. Completion of this transition is the spec's parser-resilience proof: a tailer wedged on the long line would never fire it. The session never entered waiting — the prompt forbids tools, so no permission.requested.
